faq.label: COMMON BUYER QUESTIONS
faq.title: Important answers before character development starts.
items: What do you need to quote a plush headcover?

Start with the target club type, estimated quantity, front/side/rear references, required features, logo files, intended material feel, packaging, destination and in-hands date. Pricing remains dependent on the reviewed construction and sample route.
Can you copy an existing cartoon or sports mascot?

We can work from artwork you are authorised to use. We should not copy third-party characters, team marks or protected designs without the appropriate rights. Original character development is the safer route when permission is unavailable.
Can a plush cover fit different driver sizes?
A practical fit range may be possible, but the intended club or agreed fit reference must be defined. The character volume, padding, internal depth and opening all affect fit and retention.
How are multiple character versions ordered?
Each version may introduce separate pattern, material, colour, embroidery and setup requirements. Share the quantity by character rather than only the combined total.
Will the product recover after shipping?
Packing method, pile, padding and character structure influence recovery. The sample and packaging review should include how the cover is reshaped and presented after transport.
How long does development take?

There is no universal schedule for a new three-dimensional character. Artwork readiness, complexity, material sourcing, sampling rounds, quantity, packaging and destination all affect the path. Share the required in-hands date before development begins.

design.title: Designing a Custom Plush Headcover
design.intro: A mascot, animal, object or original character has to work as both a recognisable three-dimensional form and a protective golf product. Start with the identifying features, then build the silhouette around club fit and construction.
rows: Character recognition
Silhouette, face, proportions, colour blocks and two or three indispensable features
Rank the features before adding decoration. The cover should still read clearly from several metres away and from more than one angle.
Headcover function
Target club type, opening, internal depth, retention and protective lining
A convincing character that does not fit, stay on the club or protect it is not a successful headcover.
Reference package
Front, side and rear views, colour values, logo assets and notes on what may change
One front image leaves important assumptions about depth, the back, underside and club opening.
checklist: Name the intended club type and provide a model, dimensions or fit reference where relevant.
Provide front, side and rear views; mark the character features that must not be simplified.
Share quantity, target date, destination, packaging direction and whether several character versions are planned.
faqs: Can a flat logo or mascot drawing become a plush headcover?
Yes, but it cannot simply be wrapped around a club. The artwork must be interpreted as volume, panels, seams, features and an opening while preserving the most recognisable cues.
How much detail should the first brief include?
Enough to identify the character, club type, non-negotiable features, colours, logo role and intended use. Construction details can then be reviewed through artwork and sampling.
Can several characters share one base construction?
Potentially, when the overall volume and opening are compatible. Major changes to ears, beaks, horns, faces or proportions may require different patterns and separate sample review.

materials.title: Plush Materials, Linings & Closures
materials.intro: Outer texture is only one layer of the product. Shape retention, padding, lining, club insertion and opening security should be specified together before a material is approved.
rows: Outer material
Short plush, sherpa, velour-like textile or mixed panels
Pile length changes how seams, embroidery and small facial details appear. Colour, shedding, recovery and hand-feel require review.
Shape & protection
Foam, padding or structural layers appropriate to the proposed form
Internal support helps the character retain volume, but excessive bulk can affect weight, club fit and packing.
Lining
Velvet, short plush, fleece or another agreed protective textile
Check softness, seam coverage, colour transfer risk, insertion feel and how the lining behaves around the opening.
Opening & retention
Fitted knit or sock neck, elastic route, drawcord or another reviewed construction
The opening should balance easy use with reliable retention. The suitable route depends on the club and character shape.
checklist: Describe the desired texture with a physical or photographic reference.
Confirm the club type, internal protection expectation and preferred insertion feel.
Review the outer material, structure, lining and opening on the complete sample rather than as isolated swatches.
faqs: Is longer plush always more premium?
No. Longer pile can hide seams and create softness, but it can also obscure embroidery and precise features. Material should support the character and intended brand expression.
Can different materials be mixed on one character?
Yes. Mixed pile lengths, appliqué textiles and structured panels can improve recognition, but thickness transitions, seams and colour matching need to be checked.
Is a magnetic closure required?
Not universally. Many plush covers use a fitted or sock-style opening. The appropriate retention method depends on club type, geometry, weight and intended use.

branding.title: Embroidery & Character Details
branding.intro: Small details behave differently on plush than on flat fabric. The best method is the one that keeps the character and brand readable after the material, curvature and seam plan are considered.
rows: Facial features
Embroidery, appliqué, shaped textile parts or a combined method
Eyes, mouth and expression need adequate scale and contrast. Avoid placing critical features across unstable seams or deep pile.
Brand marks
Flat or raised embroidery, woven or rubber patch, appliqué or label
Keep the logo hierarchy separate from the character features so neither becomes visually crowded.
Dimensional features
Ears, wings, horns, tails, fins or other shaped components
Each projecting feature affects balance, packing and durability. Attachment points and internal support should be visible in sample review.
Colour control
Material colour, thread, print or patch values
The same colour reference can appear different across plush, woven textile and embroidery, so the completed combination matters.
checklist: Provide original vector logos and the highest-quality character references available.
Mark which details must be dimensional and which may be embroidered or appliquéd.
Review feature position on front, profile and rear views—not only a flat front artwork.
faqs: Can very small text be embroidered on plush?
Fine text can lose clarity in pile and curvature. Simplifying the mark, increasing size, using a patch or moving it to a flatter panel may produce a better result.
Should the logo replace part of the character?
Only when it supports the intended design. Often the character establishes recognition while a separate, quieter logo area preserves brand clarity.
How are sculptural features confirmed?
Artwork communicates position and proportion, while a physical sample is the reliable point for judging projection, balance, attachment and three-dimensional recognition.

sample.title: Plush Sample Approval Checklist
sample.intro: Approve more than appearance. A useful sample review checks character recognition, club fit, retention, lining, seams, feature security, branding and packing against the written brief.
rows: Recognition & proportions
Silhouette, face, colour balance and required features from several angles
Compare the sample with the approved reference and note differences precisely instead of requesting a general improvement.
Fit & handling
Club insertion, internal depth, opening, retention, removal and bag position
Test with the intended club or an agreed fit reference. A display-only review cannot confirm daily use.
Construction
Panel symmetry, seams, pile direction, padding, lining and dimensional attachments
Check whether features recover after handling and whether internal or external seams create unwanted pressure or distortion.
Branding & packing
Logo clarity, feature alignment, colour, individual packing and carton recovery
Packing can compress plush forms. Confirm how the product is restored and presented after transport.
checklist: Use one consolidated comment list tied to dated front, side, rear and underside images.
Separate critical corrections from preferences and confirm which approved reference each comment relates to.
Recheck fit, feature security and packing after visual corrections; one change can affect another part of the product.
faqs: Is an artwork proof enough for a plush character?

Artwork is useful for colour, position and proportion, but a new three-dimensional character usually benefits from physical sample review because volume, fit and feature attachment cannot be fully confirmed on screen.
What should be measured on the sample?
Measure relevant external proportions, opening and internal depth, then test with the intended club or agreed fit reference. Measurements should support—not replace—the handling test.
What belongs in the approved sample record?
Keep the current specification, artwork, material and colour references, photographs, fit notes, packaging details and the final consolidated approval comments together.
